Create an Azure SQL Database and Connect from VS Code

Nithin Sunke · October 30, 2026 · 10 min read

A hands-on walkthrough: provision a serverless Azure SQL Database from the Azure portal, configure networking and security, then connect and query it from VS Code. Written from an Oracle DBA's point of view.

In this post
  1. What Azure SQL Database is (and isn't)
  2. Prerequisites and the free offer
  3. Create the database in the portal
  4. Verify the deployment
  5. Connect from VS Code
  6. Same thing with Azure CLI
  7. Troubleshooting
  8. Oracle to Azure SQL mental map
  9. Clean up

What Azure SQL Database is (and isn't)

Azure SQL Database is a fully managed PaaS database built on the SQL Server engine. There is nothing to install. You provision it, and Microsoft handles patching, backups, high availability and upgrades. If you come from OCI, think of it as the SQL Server equivalent of Autonomous Database.

Every database lives on a logical server. This is not a VM you log in to; it is a management and connection endpoint (<name>.database.windows.net) that holds the admin login, firewall rules and authentication settings for the databases under it.

Prerequisites and the free offer

  • An Azure subscription.
  • The Contributor, SQL DB Contributor or SQL Server Contributor role on the subscription or resource group.
  • A client tool. I use VS Code with the SQL Server (mssql) extension; SSMS or sqlcmd work too.
Free offer: each subscription can create up to 10 free serverless databases, each with 100,000 vCore seconds of compute, 32 GB of data and 32 GB of backup storage per month, for the lifetime of the subscription. Pick SQL database (Free offer) or click Apply offer on the create page.

Create the database in the portal

1Open Azure SQL Database

In the Azure portal, open All services, choose the Databases category, and select Azure SQL Database.

2Start the create wizard

On the SQL databases page, click + Create. Choose SQL database, or SQL database (Free offer) if you want the free tier applied automatically.

3Basics: project and database details

Select your subscription and create a new resource group (I used aznslabs). Enter a database name (azsqldb). The Server field is empty because there's no logical server yet, so click Create new under it.

4Create the logical server

Fill in the server details:

  • Server name: must be globally unique; it becomes nslabsazsrv01.database.windows.net.
  • Location: I chose (Asia Pacific) India South Central.
  • Authentication method: Use both SQL and Microsoft Entra authentication. Set yourself as the Entra admin and define a SQL admin login and password.

Click OK.

Microsoft recommends Entra-only authentication for production. Keeping SQL authentication enabled is convenient for labs and for tools that don't support Entra sign-in.

5Configure compute and storage

Back on the Basics tab, leave SQL elastic pool at No and click Configure database. I used:

  • Service tier: General Purpose (most budget friendly)
  • Compute tier: Serverless (billed per second for vCores used)
  • Hardware: Standard-series (Gen5)
  • Max / Min vCores: 1 / 1

Scroll down to set the auto-pause delay, the data max size (32 GB) and zone redundancy (No), then click Apply.

Save free compute: I left auto-pause disabled for this lab, but enabling it lets the database pause when idle so it doesn't burn through the monthly free vCore seconds. The trade-off is a short delay on the first connection after a pause.

6Review the Basics tab

The tab now shows the new server, Workload environment set to Development, and General Purpose – Serverless compute. For Backup storage redundancy, I picked Locally-redundant, which is the cheapest option and fine for a lab. Choose geo-redundant if you need geo-restore. Click Next: Networking.

7Networking

  • Connectivity method: Public endpoint. Use a private endpoint for production inside a VNet.
  • Allow Azure services and resources to access this server: No. This setting opens the server to any Azure resource, including other tenants', so leave it off unless you need it.
  • Add current client IP address: Yes. This creates the firewall rule your laptop needs to connect.
  • Connection policy: Default.
  • Minimum TLS version: 1.2.

I left the Security tab at its defaults. Transparent Data Encryption is on by default with service-managed keys.

8Additional settings

Under Use existing data, choose None for an empty database, Backup to restore, or Sample for AdventureWorksLT. I kept the default collation SQL_Latin1_General_CP1_CI_AS and the system default maintenance window (5pm to 8am).

Collation can't be changed after the database is created, so decide now if your application needs something other than the default.

9Review + create

Check the summary and estimated cost, then click Create. The Download a template for automation link gives you the ARM template for this exact configuration, which is handy for repeating it later.

Verify the deployment

Deployment took a couple of minutes. It creates four resources: the logical server, the database, the connection policy and the client IP firewall rule.

The database now appears under SQL databases:

Open it to see the Overview. Note the Server name (nslabsazsrv01.database.windows.net) and the Connection strings link; you'll need these to connect.

Connect from VS Code

Install the SQL Server (mssql) extension, open the SQL Server view and click Add Connection. Fill in:

FieldValue
Server namenslabsazsrv01.database.windows.net, port 1433
Authentication typeSQL Login
User name / PasswordThe server admin login created in step 4
Database nameazsqldb
EncryptMandatory
Trust server certificateUnchecked; Azure presents a valid certificate

Click Test connection, then Connect.

Run a quick query to confirm you're connected:

SELECT @@VERSION;

The version always reports 12.0.x on Azure SQL Database. That doesn't mean SQL Server 2014; the service runs the latest engine and the number is fixed for compatibility.

Load some sample data

To have something to work with, I created sample schemas (Sales, HR, Finance, Inventory, CRM and others) with related tables. Schemas in Azure SQL are namespaces inside the database, much like schemas in an Oracle PDB, but without being tied to a user.

Create an application user

Don't let applications use the server admin. Connected to azsqldb, create a contained database user, which authenticates at the database level without a server login:

CREATE USER appuser WITH PASSWORD = '<StrongPassword>';
ALTER ROLE db_datareader ADD MEMBER appuser;
ALTER ROLE db_datawriter ADD MEMBER appuser;

Same thing with Azure CLI

The portal steps above map to a few CLI commands, which you can run from Cloud Shell:

RG=aznslabs
LOC=centralindia
SERVER=nslabsazsrv01
DB=azsqldb
ADMIN=sqladmin
PASS='<StrongPassword>'

az group create -n $RG -l $LOC

az sql server create -g $RG -n $SERVER -l $LOC \
  --admin-user $ADMIN --admin-password "$PASS"

MYIP=$(curl -s https://api.ipify.org)
az sql server firewall-rule create -g $RG -s $SERVER -n AllowMyIp \
  --start-ip-address $MYIP --end-ip-address $MYIP

az sql db create -g $RG -s $SERVER -n $DB \
  --edition GeneralPurpose --compute-model Serverless \
  --family Gen5 --capacity 1 --auto-pause-delay 60

Or connect from the command line with sqlcmd:

sqlcmd -S tcp:nslabsazsrv01.database.windows.net,1433 -d azsqldb \
  -U <admin> -P '<password>' -N -Q "SELECT DB_NAME(), @@VERSION"

Troubleshooting

SymptomFix
Client with IP address 'x.x.x.x' is not allowed to access the serverYour public IP changed or isn't allowed. Open the SQL server → Security → Networking and add your client IPv4 address.
Timeout or network errorOutbound TCP 1433 is blocked on your network or VPN, or public access is disabled on the server.
Login failedCheck the login name, the password and that you're connecting to the right database. Contained users must specify the database.
First query after idle is slow or times outA serverless database with auto-pause resumes on the first connection. Retry after about a minute.

Oracle to Azure SQL mental map

OracleAzure SQL Database
CDB / listener endpointLogical server
PDBDatabase
SchemaSchema inside the database (e.g. dbo, Sales)
RMAN backupsAutomatic backups with point-in-time restore (7–35 days)
Data GuardActive geo-replication / failover groups
TDE walletTDE on by default; service-managed or customer-managed keys in Key Vault

Clean up

When you're done, delete the resource group. This removes the server, the database and the firewall rules in one go:

az group delete -n aznslabs

Wrapping up

In about ten minutes you have a managed, encrypted SQL Server database with automatic backups, reachable only from your own IP, and costing nothing under the free offer.
